records.summary: KernelStore is large, central, and currently intentional as the product-record substrate.
records.rationale: Large-class pressure should not automatically split the store. The important question is whether higher-level publication helpers and provenance concepts keep record construction precise and explainable.
guidance: Treat KernelStore size as intentional unless new work adds unrelated policy or source-specific publication behavior.
Prefer improving product-record publication helpers before pushing more responsibilities into KernelStore.

Use KernelStore mark/dispose only for query-boundary reclamation of answer-local records and sidecars; app-world invalidation still needs an explicit epoch policy. Disposal summaries should include reclaimed record-handle character mass so one-off answer telemetry can separate logical disposal from transient handle-string bulk.

KernelHandleFactory compacts broad store/local key parts because handles are hot session links, not semantic payload. If a consumer needs more readable identity, add the source/product/detail field that owns that meaning rather than widening handle strings globally.

Use fieldProvenanceWhenDistinct when a materializer has owning source/product provenance plus optional field-specific witnesses. Repeating the owner provenance as field provenance is usually representation noise unless the field-provenance array intentionally carries configured-field presence.
Use product.vocabulary and product.architecture kernel-records when judging whether record shapes are coherent.

anchors.summary: Central kernel product-record store.
Store-local handle minting and compaction policy.
Vocabulary rows that define record/product language.

records.summary: AuthoredSourceTextCache is the shared convenience reader over one captured project-input generation for source slicing and cursor coordinate conversion.
records.rationale: Template markup can be decoded or source-mapped while diagnostics, overlays, cursor inquiries, and edit surfaces still need exact authored HTML or TypeScript host text. Centralizing raw reads, generation-bounded memoization, and line math prevents API/template-local filesystem readers, stale source values, and offset requirements from drifting.
guidance: Use AuthoredSourceTextCache when a product already has a source path/span and needs to slice raw authored text or convert between offset and line/character coordinates.
Use resolveSemanticSourceCursor at the public query boundary before any cursor containment operation. Line and character are the complete contract; an explicit offset is only a caller optimization.

Use AuthoredSourceTextCache for app-source text scans over the captured project-input host, including boot project-shape source-signal scans; package/tsconfig discovery and evaluation module-host reads share that generation but retain their own domain APIs.
Do not replace this with TemplateSource.markup unless the consumer only needs decoded compiler input and not authored-source coordinates.

Resource convergence should use the same cache for conventional/imported external template text so template-file reads, decoded metadata, diagnostics, cursor loci, and overlays stay on one authored-text boundary.
I18n imported JSON key spans should use the evaluator asset-module helper over this cache so source addresses point at authored JSON properties rather than the generated module wrapper.
Use product.architecture source-file read pressure before adding new direct readFileSync, existsSync, or line-offset helpers in semantic-runtime.

Project-input generations are the source/configuration epoch. Construct this cache over the captured host and advance the owning authority after input changes instead of adding local defensive reads in diagnostics, overlays, completion, references, or rename.

anchors.summary: Shared authored source text cache and line/offset helper boundary.
Normalizes line/character-only public query cursors before offset containment.
Overlay expression projector slices authored source through the shared cache.
Template diagnostics and cursor paths use the shared cache for source text.
Resource convergence reads imported/conventional external HTML through the shared cache before metadata stripping.
Asset module source-span helper maps generated JSON module nodes back through the shared authored source cache.
Product architecture pressure prints source-file read pressure from call-site rows.

records.summary: OpenSeam carries a primary unresolved site plus optional reasonSources for adjacent source/evidence sites that contributed individual reason kinds.
records.rationale: Router href target pressure exposed the shape: the seam is correctly owned by the dynamic href value, but `router-href-click-interception-target-open` is contributed by the host target attribute. The kernel now has an OpenSeam.reasonSources carrier, router dynamic href seams publish source-bearing reason rows for the value, externality, and target-open facts, and authoring repair suggestions can choose action targets from those rows. Similar multi-site reasons can appear in binding value channels, observer selection, and framework error projections, so new consumers should extend the shared reason-source primitive instead of adding caller-local side tables.
guidance: Treat `OpenSeam.addressHandle` as the primary unresolved seam site, not proof that every `reasonKind` came from the same source span.
When a repair or diagnostic needs to act on one reason inside a multi-reason seam, use `OpenSeam.reasonSources` and API `reasonSources` rows before adding feature-local evidence tables.

API `reasonSources` rows should carry query-time `sourceRange` when their address resolves to authored text. Keep line/column derivation out of durable kernel records; the kernel owns address/evidence handles and the API owns public location projection.
Keep compact open-seam summaries stable for routing, but preserve exact reason-level provenance through structured rows when the product needs edit targets or hover explanation.

Producer-owned reason kinds should be carried into OpenSeam at publication time. Static evaluator seams now prove this path through `EvaluationOpenSeam.reasonKinds`; extend producer threading before adding downstream classifiers.

When one semantic layer wraps lower-level open seams into a higher product boundary, carry existing `reasonKinds` through the intermediate carrier before publication. `ConfigurationRecognitionOpen` and `RegistrationRecognitionOpen` preserve evaluator reasons for this purpose; add producer-specific reason taxonomy only when the higher layer owns a genuinely new reason.
Every published OpenSeam now requires at least one typed reason. Repair a missing reason at the producing authority; do not recover it from prose in a public projection.

Boundary classification must not fabricate causality from a symptom-level reason. Use `cause-unresolved` when a reason such as missing static slot/member value or generic abrupt completion does not prove one boundary, then split or enrich the producer vocabulary before assigning a narrower cause.

The 2026-07-31 broad public-quality replay closed the former reasonless producer census and verifies evidence-only versus product pressure, multi-owner conservation, exact root sites, and typed summary clusters.

Public summary answers distinguish raw cause counts, exact authored-site counts, and affected product/materialization counts structurally. Raw, site, and summary rows derive from one causal projection fact set rather than from one another.

Router dynamic href target-open pressure is the first proof lane: `contract:router-dynamic-pattern` expects the `router-href-click-interception-target-open` reason source and repair action target to be source-bearing.
Do not split one coherent runtime boundary into several open seams just to get per-reason source addresses; that loses the fact that the reasons describe one unresolved runtime decision.

anchors.summary: Current first-class open seam record with a primary address/evidence handle, reasonKinds, and optional reasonSources.
Shared source-backed open-seam publication primitive.
Evaluator-local seam carrier that preserves producer reason kinds until kernel publication.
Binding data-flow boundary maps checker-owned typed expression-open kinds into producer-owned seam reasons without reparsing prose.
Broad pressure-fixture sweep for public open-seam trust: raw/site/summary totals, reasonKinds, source ranges, static-evaluation origin uniqueness, and paging completeness.

Contract proving repeated derivation rows collapse into unique authored sites while summary totals, raw display samples, source roles, application roles, static-evaluation origins, reason filters, and continuations stay public.
Contract proving evaluator-produced open seams preserve reason kinds through public seam projections.
Contract proving evaluator reason kinds survive the configuration product-boundary handoff.
Contract proving router dynamic href reasonSources preserve source-bearing reason provenance and authored source ranges.
Router href click-interception facts can contribute reason kinds from host attributes and router options.
Diagnostics-to-action owns future repair/action classification before host edit planning spends OpenSeam source evidence.
Pressure fixture now includes a dynamic href seam whose target-open reason is contributed by the host target attribute.

records.summary: ProductDetailCatalog is the product-envelope admission wrapper over the shared in-memory detail catalog.
records.rationale: Rich TypeScript checker objects, framework models, and current-run materializer details do not belong in durable kernel records, but inquiry and downstream materializers need typed access to them. ProductDetailCatalog owns product-envelope validation and weak binding while DetailCatalog owns the storage, lifetime, mutation, and detail-kind mechanics shared with product-owned hot children.
guidance: Start here when a materializer or inquiry needs to attach, read, or enumerate rich details for a materialized product.
Define a ProductDetailSlot for a product-owned contract instead of using generic payload escape hatches.
Keep duplicate-detail and product-kind checks strict so product details remain tied to committed durable products.
Keep storage and lifetime mechanics in DetailCatalog. ProductDetailCatalog should own only product-envelope admission and normalization semantics; do not fork another catalog implementation.
ProductDetailEntry carries the owning MaterializedProduct envelope; derive envelope facts there before copying product, identity, address, or provenance handles into a detail shape.

Use ProductDetailCatalog.addAll(...) and addAllIfAbsent(...) for homogeneous materializer emission row families whose details already carry product handles; keep nullable or conditional detail attachment explicit at the call site.

ProductDetailCatalog participates in kernel mark/dispose so query-local product details can be reclaimed with their envelopes; durable app-world product invalidation still belongs to an app epoch policy.

Use the opt-in detail-density telemetry lane before changing product-detail retention. If direct string mass is mostly handle fields, treat that as representation or inquiry-depth pressure instead of dropping navigable handles.
Use unique direct string counts beside total direct string characters before assuming string repetition is the memory bug; detail-density is logical payload evidence, not exact heap ownership.

Use the detail-density envelope-echo rows to distinguish product envelope duplication from new semantic payload. A high echo count points at derived-reference or query-depth design, not at a random source-payload blob.

ProductDetailCatalog binds detail objects to their owning MaterializedProduct envelope and normalizes exact own-field echoes such as productHandle, identityHandle, sourceAddressHandle, addressHandle, primaryIdentityHandle, and provenanceHandle into non-enumerable envelope-backed accessors. If detail-density still reports envelope echoes, check whether the detail bypassed ProductDetailCatalog or whether the field is deliberately not the owning envelope.

Use non-envelope handle rows before refactoring detail classes: they usually represent cross-product navigation links, while envelope echoes may be derivable from the ProductDetailEntry or owning MaterializedProduct envelope.
Use non-handle string rows to see scalar payload after handle-shaped strings are removed from the logical mass.

anchors.summary: Hot typed product-detail catalog.
Typed product-detail slot contract.
Bulk detail attachment for homogeneous emitted product-detail row families.

records.summary: HotDetailCatalog is the product-owned child-detail admission wrapper over the shared in-memory detail catalog.
records.rationale: Memory telemetry showed that some rich child surfaces, especially TypeChecker member rows owned by projected type shapes, are useful to in-process analysis but too numerous or too low-level to justify their own product envelopes. HotDetailCatalog keeps those children typed, explicitly owned, mark/disposable, and query-visible without promoting them into durable kernel products.
guidance: Start here when a materializer needs typed in-memory detail access but the detail has no independent product-kind navigation, claims, provenance, or cross-inquiry durability requirement.

Prefer ProductDetailCatalog when the detail expands its own committed MaterializedProduct; prefer HotDetailCatalog when the detail is a lightweight child of another product and should follow that product or publication epoch's lifetime.

Keep hot detail slots explicit and documented with their owner product kind, and publish each child with its exact owner product handle. Do not use hot details as generic payload storage for facts that should become kernel products or claims.
Use HotDetailHandle for child lookup. Never put a hot-detail key in a ProductHandle field or expose it as a durable product in public contracts.
Product replacement must refresh retained child entries with the committed post-state owner envelope and reject replacement while a foreign publication owns a hot child.
HotDetailCatalog participates in kernel mark/dispose so query-local hot rows can be reclaimed with answer-local products.

Use detail-density telemetry to distinguish hot-detail object count from direct string/array field mass; TypeChecker member hot details often retain handle-shaped navigation strings even when they avoid durable product envelopes.

Hot details have an explicit owning MaterializedProduct but no product envelope of their own. Their exact handle/detailHandle echo is derivable; declaration, source, and cross-product handles remain current-epoch navigation.

anchors.summary: Epoch-local typed hot detail catalog.
Typed hot-detail slot contract.

records.summary: Kernel sidecar indexes are named acceleration structures that mirror kernel/product-detail lifetimes.
records.rationale: Query-local products and hot details may be disposed after an answer is shaped, but private indexes can otherwise retain stale TypeChecker carriers, members, and other rich detail objects. Registering sidecar indexes with KernelStore makes their lifetime explicit and visible in telemetry.
guidance: Start here when a cache/index points at product details, hot details, TypeChecker carriers, or query-local materialized products.
Register store-local acceleration indexes with KernelStore.registerSidecarIndex(...) instead of hiding them in package-level WeakMaps with no disposal contract.
Use sidecar index telemetry rows to check whether an index is retaining answer-local work after QueryClaimGraph disposal.
The app-analysis project authority registry is a sidecar because lifecycle-owned publications remain semantic truth; disposal prunes authorities whose committed generations have been retired.
Do not turn sidecar indexes into semantic storage; durable semantics still belong in kernel records, claims, identities, products, product details, or hot details with explicit lifetimes.

anchors.summary: Registers named store-local indexes that prune on kernel disposal.
Current project-generation authority registry registered as a disposable kernel sidecar index.

anchors.summary: Kernel docs describing sidecar indexes as named disposable acceleration structures.
Contract proving canonical TypeChecker projections follow kernel detail lifetime without a duplicate sidecar identity map.

records.summary: Kernel handles are compactable session transport links, not durable semantic identities.
records.rationale: Telemetry showed recursive local-key handles retaining millions of repeated characters in hot app worlds. The kernel already stores semantic identity, source coordinates, product kind, and provenance in typed records, so handle strings can trade some readability for memory without becoming semantic truth.
guidance: Do not parse kernel handles to recover product kind, source identity, route keys, DI keys, or type identity; read the typed records instead.
When a consumer needs stable identity across stores, model that as a domain field or semantic identity rather than relying on handle text.
Store-key handle parts may compact more aggressively than local-key parts because the store/workspace identity is repeated on every handle and is not the semantic local key.
Keep compact handle readable prefixes short. The hash guards store-local uniqueness, while typed records own semantic identity and explanation.
Treat new long handle families as local-key design pressure first, then handle compaction pressure only when the handle is legitimately transport-only.
Use semantic-runtime telemetry handle-character breakdowns before widening handle compaction or adding per-family string interning.

Use source-span role and source-file role breakdowns before changing address storage; exact source-span duplication was low on the mixed-form canary, so broad address savings likely need representation/inquiry-policy work rather than simple de-duplication.

anchors.summary: Serializes compactable store-local kernel handles.

Telemetry row that reports handle-character pressure.

records.summary: Source-backed diagnostics that become semantic issue products should reuse the kernel issue-publication primitive.
records.rationale: Dialog, fetch-client, state, and validation issue publishers share the same evidence/provenance/identity/materialized-product/materialization envelope while retaining domain-specific issue objects and identity records. The shared primitive keeps product publication coherent without forcing every package to grow one-off publication classes.
guidance: Use publishIssueProduct when a diagnostic is a materialized semantic product with domain-owned issue details.
Keep source-span creation in the caller when the caller owns exact authored source ranges; pass the resulting address handle into the issue product publication.
Use issue-publication type aliases or object literals for pure publication envelopes; add a class only when the publication object has behavior or state across calls.
If a new issue identity kind is added, make sure KernelStore indexes that identity kind in both pending batch validation and committed record expansion.

records.summary: Authored source-token facts should publish source address, evidence, and provenance together.
records.rationale: The bindable alias and HTML source-locus canaries showed that carrying only SourceSpanAddressHandle fields is enough for editor spans but not enough for the kernel provenance and future invalidation story. Field-specific source facts need a single witness unit: the authored source span address, evidence that observes that span, and provenance that points at that evidence. Otherwise IDE surfaces and kernel fieldProvenance can drift into parallel islands.
guidance: Use sourceSpanEvidenceForSite when an authored token becomes a durable product fact, edit target, or fieldProvenance witness; syntax-specific helpers should derive a SourceSpanSite and delegate to that kernel publication primitive.
Keep address-only helpers for carriers whose product provenance already explains the field, or consumers that only need a span and do not publish product field provenance.
Do not mechanically add fieldProvenance entries that repeat the owning source provenance; fieldProvenance should identify distinct field witnesses or intentional field presence.

HTML element tag names and attribute name/value fields have narrower authored witnesses than their node or attribute carriers, so they publish distinct field provenance; parser-owned expression tokens remain lightweight projected spans unless they become durable product fields.

Treat this as a bridge rule for the grand incremental compiler: source addresses locate authored facts, evidence/provenance explain why the fact exists, and epoch/session invalidation remains a separate freshness policy until dependency coverage is complete.

anchors.summary: Shared kernel publication primitive for exact source address, evidence, and provenance records.
TypeScript resource-source adapter that derives a source site and delegates to the kernel publication primitive.
HTML materializer publishes distinct tag-name and attribute-field witnesses while retaining broader node carriers.
Embedded field-specific provenance entries on semantic product records.
Shared lookup helper for field-specific provenance entries.
Bindable source fields point at the same witnesses as their exact source-address handles.

records.summary: Kernel computations validate typed outer and logical-child reads inside one sealed atomic replacement of complete owned publication closures.
records.rationale: The same-runtime app-analysis front door proves complete static-evaluation, resource, DI, template, observation, state, capability, and router fan-in replacement against production materializers. A replacement candidate is a logical next world, not an overlay on its own previous output: the active publication hides the prior owned manifest, exposes current run writes, and is the shared read, commit, and telemetry authority. Exact committed record/detail reads and exact computation outputs share technical read keys. Logical children retain the writer and candidate revision of each staged output beneath that one outer transaction, preserving exact child-to-child edges and unresolved aggregate blockers without inventing independently committing producers. KernelStore still performs the single prevalidated replacement across records and sidecars, while QueryClaimGraph remains the answer-retention layer above product computation.
guidance: Use a stable semantic computation locus for reconciliation; never make a source path, run sequence, compiler cohort, or copied input object the computation identity when the owning semantic definition is stable.

A replacement run must not read its own prior publication as upstream state. Hide the previous owned record/detail closure, restage every still-current output, and let omitted outputs withdraw at commit.
Publish the complete owned record, product-detail, and hot-detail closure through one KernelPublicationPlan. Do not patch an old publication or maintain a second ownership list in a materializer.

Use the active KernelPublicationContext for nested materialization, candidate-aware record/source/materialization enumeration, TypeChecker declaration/source lookup, DI identity lookup, and any other same-generation read. Reading KernelStore directly inside a staged run can silently omit candidate records or borrow the prior generation from the replacement closure.

The staged record/detail maps are the candidate read authority, the final commit payload, and the phase-telemetry source. Seal them behind mutation-free views and let final comparison consume those exact normalized indexes; do not rebuild a second map set or sample the committed store to describe an atomic candidate.

Authenticate staged replacement with one single-use final candidate bound to the exact KernelStore and prior frozen manifest that minted it. Do not accept a caller-supplied prior manifest, remint authority to attach consumed lifetime, or replay an empty candidate against the shared empty manifest. Raw KernelPublicationPlan replacement remains valid for genuinely non-staged operations such as exact generation retirement. Advance the complete owned closure to the youngest positive dependency lifetime, including positive rows returned by an unresolved aggregate read, so an older lineage cannot survive disposal after consuming answer-local truth. During selective disposal, retain active positive exact record/detail inputs and the positive committed rows captured by aggregate reads as well as active outputs and structural references. Enumerate active manifests so empty replaceable closures retire too, including the owned empty replacement created by exact generation retirement. Capture exact foreign detail admission entries, mutation revisions, and lifetimes during staging; apply fallible detail-field normalization as one reversible descriptor transaction before live mutation. Fresh or exactly equivalent candidate details may receive provisional weak bindings so final validators see the post-state graph; rejection restores those bindings and descriptors. A staged read must not rebind an already committed detail to a changed envelope. Reusing a committed detail is readable only under an exactly equivalent candidate product envelope; semantic or witness movement requires a fresh generation-local detail. Retained committed bindings refresh only during successful admission. A failed staged write poisons the run; never commit its accepted prefix.

Register every positive and negative dependency read at the operation that consumes it. ComputationRun exact record/product-detail/hot-detail reads do this by construction and exclude candidate or hidden prior output; positive borrowed IfAbsent admissions are reads. After authoritative admission decisions exist, remove a read whose key became this generation's own output, but retain borrowed IfAbsent reads because they have no output decision. Do not infer a preparation read later from an output reference.

Index committed technical outputs through the same exact read keys used by reverse readers. Product-detail and hot-detail keys identify the one catalog occupancy by handle; requested and actual detail kinds are revision facets, not separate dependency identities. Run owner-specific producer checks through KernelStore.replaceOwnedPublicationCandidate after complete staged preparation and before its callback-free mutation tail; allocate a new publication lifetime only after that preflight. Use raw replaceOwnedPublication only for non-staged lifecycle operations such as retirement. Producer ownership changes only with successful publication replacement and clears on exact retirement or lifetime disposal; semantic produces-product claims remain a separate topology vocabulary.

Use ComputationRun.withChild only for synchronous logical preparation beneath the outer transaction. Child callbacks cannot commit or abort, and failures or asynchronous returns poison the outer candidate. Child scopes are flat: lexical nesting changes the active writer but does not create hierarchy. Every admitted output has exactly one child writer; retain unmigrated work under the explicit remainder child instead of leaving it unattributed.

KernelStoreBatch takes ownership of normalized record values by sealing record identity, classification, and embedded structural collections before immediate or staged publication can capture revisions or expose sibling reads. Keep rich detail payloads outside this record rule; their mutable domain objects remain protected by canonical closure projection and post-callback revalidation.

Seal normalized records, publication wrappers, read metadata, normalized locus identity, committed lifecycle state, and the complete candidate graph before entering replacement. A committed locus retains only kind, reconciliationKey, and summary; encode domain identity in the key instead of depending on a concrete locus prototype or caller payload. Restore superseded candidate leases before entering the store so abandoned cleanup cannot fail after durable admission. Finish record/detail comparison, fallible binding preparation, and reversible descriptor normalization inside the store reentrancy barrier, then pass one frozen decision set to final input, child-read, and producer validation. Revalidate normalized descriptors and reproject every rich detail structural closure after external validators; both operations may invoke candidate-owned JavaScript. Then inspect one nominal composite GenerationCurrentnessWitness over the exact run and every guarded input generation through kernel-private monotonic clocks before entering the callback-free mutation tail. Do not add another callback, assume projector purity, or collapse semantic input equality into this generation proof: exact source/configuration values remain typed computation reads, while editor and host source events advance project-input authority. Keep transient publication-view currentness separate from GenerationAuthority so a finished run, poisoned staging context, or eternal store cannot masquerade as a witnessed durable generation. Reject payload mutation instead of admitting an object whose reads and retention describe an older closure. Restore candidate descriptors and provisional weak bindings when final preflight rejects. Validators may read the sealed candidate through the committing run, but they cannot register new observations, enter child scopes, publish, or mutate the store. Rich typed detail payloads remain domain objects and are not recursively frozen by the kernel.

Retain candidate-local absence and the final staged writer/revision for exact child reads. A sibling must not fill an absence or replace a consumed candidate unnoticed. Every IfAbsent attempt consumes one occupancy: foreign entries remain committed reads, coalesced candidate entries become producer edges, and a later stronger writer rejects an earlier prepared conditional admission.

Project publication references as structural dependencies from the projector-owned canonical closure over record, product-detail, and hot-detail surfaces. The projector deduplicates, sorts, and freezes once; the slot preserves that exact closure, while final replacement independently reprojects it after external callbacks. Product- and hot-detail planners are the sole admission authority; final replacement consumes their prepared result in one graph pass that validates references and computes external lifetime. A losing IfAbsent proposal contributes neither its payload closure nor its proposed envelope edge, while the borrowed occupancy contributes its exact committed lifetime. Do not classify admission again in a parallel graph walk. Structural references preserve referential integrity, child topology, transitive retention, and withdrawal safety, but do not claim that the target value was consumed. A semantic consumer must still register an exact or candidate read at the operation that spends the target value.

Keep stable detail identity in inert per-domain descriptors and executable dependency projection in ProductDetailSlot or HotDetailSlot. Cross-domain projectors import descriptors or cycle-neutral structural-reference functions, never another domain's live slot catalog. FieldProvenance is epistemic lineage, not a substitute dependency graph; promote a compact logical reference to exact occupancy only when its producer contract guarantees that sidecar in the same atomic plan.

Do not guess exact detail occupancy from a carrier that spans multiple epistemic forms. BindingScopeReference currently represents both durable emitted scopes and speculative unpublished handles, while RouteConfigReference spans authored contributions and effective configs; split or discriminate those carriers before promoting their handles to rich-detail dependencies.

ComputationChildState.hasOnlyRevisionedReads means only that no unresolved aggregate closure was consumed. Carry additionally requires singleton topology, stable producer ownership, current exact/materialization dependencies, compatible structural targets, and retained decision preview; the flag alone never proves safe reuse.

Do not call aggregate enumeration complete by registering only returned positive handles. Whole-store, whole-slot, source-file-index, compiler-world membership, and materialization scans require domain-owned membership, order, absence, and closure revisions. Until then, keep the read open while promoting outputs to the youngest lifetime among positive committed rows it returned.

Keep exactly one ComputationLifecycleRegistry per KernelStore. Lifetime disposal must retire the exact committed manifest capability, clear outer and child read/producer indexes, and supersede any run prepared before the reclaimed publication disappeared, including an empty committed closure.

Keep lifecycle observability non-retaining: retain only the latest transition per stable locus, do not journal retirement withdrawals, capture rebased validation callbacks instead of predecessor observations, and share immutable output descriptors between outer and child closures. Historical telemetry or future independent scheduler delivery must own an explicit bounded lifetime.

Admit retained domain object graphs once per computation run and domain through ComputationLifecycleRegistry; domain-local authority objects must not independently decide whether the same committed publication can become current twice.

Rebase equivalent consumer input manifests through the target SemanticRuntimeProjectInputGeneration's shared captured host. The target generation owns one immutable value/read table; do not reconstruct retained-value hosts or let evaluator and checker consumers recapture the same logical read independently. Exact pull validation compares the newly read value with that retained immutable value and computes a changed revision only when equality fails; do not hash unchanged content after discarding the stronger value witness. ComputationReadValidationScope may share validation only within one synchronous proof, while candidate acquisition and final commit always start separate proofs.

Treat exact source-file content and existence as ordinary project-input reads. The former source-snapshot authority duplicated that currentness boundary after its production computation was deleted; do not recreate a parallel source authority. Hash source text only when a retained semantic product needs a compact content identity beyond the exact read.
Use markLifetime for reclamation boundaries and markObservation for telemetry deltas. Publication replacement preserves lifetime identity while advancing mutation observation order.

KernelStore.publish is an immediate first-publication boundary, not a recomputation protocol. Route its records and details through the same all-or-nothing replacement preflight, but do not allocate a lifetime when the one-shot publication owns nothing. Empty replaceable store or computation generations still own exact manifests. Do not approximate replacement with cleanup calls or split one replaceable owner across legacy immediate publications.

Keep QueryClaimGraph focused on answer shape, lazy materialization, retention, and answer-side disposal. Do not move durable product dependency ownership or computation invalidation into the answer graph.

The first production child pilot is the complete recursive authored-template compiler front door across every cohort for one stable owner. Source and compiler observations plus parsing/lowering outputs are family-owned. Before shared runtime and TypeChecker analysis, re-observe the live compiler authority and consume exact resource-definition, compiled-template, render-target, instruction-sequence, instruction, compiler-world, resource-scope, Rendering, TemplateCompiler, resource-resolver, expression-parser, AttrMapper, binding-command-resolver, and authored-attribute-syntax products plus typed details. This explicitly includes local-template definitions and instruction details rather than treating references from a stable compiled-template envelope as value reads. Shared runtime and TypeChecker analysis remains in the explicit broad post-template child until its SCC schedule, expression-world membership, and cross-family bound-controller edges earn narrower owners. That broad child may itself carry only with zero open reads, exact evaluator/checker/front-door identity, and successful compiler-read rebase. None and needsCompile=false are no-output states, not alternate compile paths.

The measured activation layer is the existing deterministic carry-or-compile family loop over a pre-template -> independent family* -> post-template star. It matches cold semantic truth across no-op, source-edit, withdrawal, and reintroduction generations while retaining unrelated families and carrying the exact broad post-template closure when all gates hold. A generic scheduler is not justified until production evidence contains real sibling ordering, cycles, or fixed points; semantic/witness propagation cutoff and finer post-template ownership remain later gates.

Nominal canonical structural closure over record, product-detail, and hot-detail occupancies.

Normalized-record ownership boundary that seals record identity and structure before immediate or staged visibility.

Production complete app-analysis closure and authored-template source reads admitted to the computation lifecycle.
Stable child locus for one authored template owner across every compiler cohort and recursive local template.
Production template compiler-front-door family pilot with project-owned runtime and checker analysis.
Immutable compiler-world authority and typed positive/negative read registration.
Generation-owned immutable host-value table and authoritative consumer read-scope rebase boundary.
Kernel publication, exact and child producer/read indexing, candidate read-view, marker, and aggregate-closure doctrine.
Template family child boundary and the project-owned runtime/checker remainder.

records.summary: One authored template owner forms one logical compiler-front-door child across all cohorts and recursive local templates inside the atomic app computation.
records.rationale: A local template is one authored resource declaration shared by every compiler cohort, while compiler worlds and compiled products are cohort-derived. The production app computation stages one child per stable authored owner, compiles every admitted app and authoring cohort plus recursive local templates under that child, and keeps store commit atomic at the outer app boundary. Shared runtime and TypeChecker analysis remains post-template-owned until its cross-family schedule earns narrower owners.
guidance: Key a template-family child by project plus stable authored owner. Source paths, declaration ordinals, compiler cohorts, and run IDs are observed or derived facts, not family identity.

Treat the immutable compiler-cohort project plan as complete candidate authority. Share local definitions, bindables, and source products once; retain separate compiler worlds, compilation units, and compiled templates per cohort.

Use one logical child of the production app ComputationRun for the complete recursive compiler front door. Child manifests own reads and outputs but never commit independently from the outer app transaction.

Route exact authored-source reads, local definitions, generated compiler worlds, compiler observations, parsing, lowering, and compiled-template products through the family child's KernelPublicationContext.

Before project-owned runtime and checker analysis, re-observe live compiler authority and exact-read every resource definition, compiler product, service detail, and authored attribute syntax that runtime analysis consumes.

Retain both parent and active compiler worlds for each recursive emission. Pure current projections may be distinct objects with the same stable handle; validate handles and current semantics rather than object identity.
The former focused family producer and dynamic cohort authorities are deleted. Do not recreate a second family production path.

Owner-local materialization membership and pre/family/post phase ownership are revisioned. Carry a family only through ComputationRun.tryCarryChild after exact rebase and retained dependency preview; otherwise rerun it.

The measured activation layer is the existing deterministic family loop over a pre-template -> independent family* -> post-template star. Only Retain cuts propagation; open closure, RefreshWitness, nontrivial SCCs, or failed rebase rerun.

Keep app-root compiler worlds under pre-template until they have an independently reusable closure. Computation children are flat, so lexically nesting an app-root child would create a sibling SCC rather than hierarchy.

anchors.summary: Stable child identity for one authored template owner.
Production family compiler front door and carry/rebase integration.
Current parent and derived compiler-world projection authority.

records.summary: Lightweight child details have explicit product ownership and their own handle kind without becoming kernel products.
records.rationale: The TypeMember memory compression moved high-volume members out of MaterializedProduct envelopes but left product-shaped handles, false ProductHandle fields, duplicated catalog machinery, and no enforceable owner edge. That incomplete migration let child ownership drift from product replacement and allowed synthetic members to escape without catalog admission. Product details and hot children now share storage mechanics while retaining strict, different admission contracts.
guidance: Use ProductDetailSlot when one rich detail hydrates its own MaterializedProduct envelope; use HotDetailSlot only for a lightweight child whose exact owner product kind is known.
Every hot-detail publication must name the owner ProductHandle and a branded HotDetailHandle. Never cast or store a HotDetailHandle as ProductHandle.
Derive a synthetic hot child's handle from its exact owner product and semantic child key. Caller-local projection seeds must not duplicate children under one owner.
Public and scope contracts that need both lanes should carry ownerProductHandle and detailHandle separately; semantic identity still belongs in identity records.
Product replacement refreshes retained child entries with the actual committed post-state owner envelope and refuses replacement while a foreign publication owns a hot child.

A detail publication that attaches to a product from another publication inherits the owner's record lifetime. Selective disposal roots active detail-owner products and their transitive normalized-record closure; it must not retain a detail after reclaiming the owner's identity, address, or provenance.
Keep storage, detail-kind indexing, lifetime, and mutation mechanics in DetailCatalog. ProductDetailCatalog and HotDetailCatalog own only their distinct binding and admission rules.
Do not restore one MaterializedProduct per TypeMember unless a future product genuinely needs independent claims, provenance, navigation, or cross-inquiry durability.

anchors.summary: Shared storage and lifetime core for both detail catalog wrappers.
Typed child-detail contract with an explicit owner product kind.
Atomic publication boundary that validates owner post-state and foreign-child lifetimes.
Product-owned TypeMember detail carrying HotDetailHandle rather than ProductHandle.
Scope slot contract that names declaration and current-type member detail handles honestly.

records.summary: Materialization-to-seam edges distinguish product pressure from raw analysis evidence.
records.rationale: A 189-fixture audit found 444 open seams after configuration and DI causality repair. All 369 domain product-attempt seams are now retained by MaterializationRecord.openSeamHandles; the remaining 75 unowned seams are exactly raw evaluator evidence (dynamic calls, unresolved identifiers, unsupported statements, and dynamic mutation). Source containment locates an unresolved observation but does not prove that a semantic product spent it. Product-bearing partial attempts retain the seam on their existing materialization, while attempts that fail before producing a product publish an empty-product materialization owned by the exact semantic identity or source span.
guidance: Do not add an owner field to OpenSeam. One seam may affect several products, and product relevance is the inbound MaterializationRecord.openSeamHandles relation.
When a partial semantic product exists, attach its seam handles to that product's existing materialization instead of publishing a parallel failure materialization.
When a genuine semantic product attempt fails before producing a product, publish an empty-product materialization owned by the exact operation identity or source span.
Keep raw evaluator seams unowned until a domain materializer spends them. Evaluator coverage boundaries are analysis evidence, not automatically diagnostics, IDE pressure, or AOT blockers.

Do not derive product pressure from source-file or span containment. Public inquiry should project ownership-derived product pressure separately from queryable analysis evidence, without deleting either family.
Consumer consequence remains policy: IDE, MCP, diagnostics, and AOT may interpret the same product-owned seam differently. Do not put severity, actionability, or blocksAot flags in the kernel seam.

Use recordsForSourceOpenMaterialization only for source-backed failed product attempts; continue using recordsForSourceOpenSeam for raw evidence or when an enclosing product materialization will retain the returned handle.

Run the focused open-seam materialization test and the broad ownership audit when adding a new domain seam family. An unowned domain attempt or an automatically owned evaluator seam is a causal-model regression.

anchors.summary: Canonical product/claim/open-seam ownership relation for one materialization attempt.
Source-backed empty-product materialization primitive for genuine failed attempts.
Product-bearing binding attempts retain their open seams on the existing target/source materialization.
Targetless DI registration spending publishes a configuration-step-owned empty-product materialization.
Renderer failures retain exact instruction, sequence, target, or controller ownership.
Focused cross-domain proof that product attempts are owned while raw evaluator evidence remains unowned.

anchors.heading: Record Families
anchors.summary: Kernel rules for raw seams, empty-product failures, and product-bearing partial materializations.

records.summary: Child carry rebases exact dependencies through one atomic publication authority, and rich-detail slots classify fresh semantic versus witness closure without weakening structural lifetime.
records.rationale: Selective activation must preserve the same read, producer, comparison, reference, and lifetime truth as an ordinary rerun. Carry is therefore an explicit kernel operation over one prior declared singleton child, not a domain cache hit. Rich-detail comparison remains slot-owned, while exact structural references remain the referential-integrity and lifetime authority rather than semantic value reads; a changed closure can refresh witnesses or replace semantics but can never retain an incumbent object with stale references.
guidance: Use ComputationRun.tryCarryChild only before candidate work starts and only for a prior declared singleton child with revisioned reads and stable producer ownership.
Rebase exact reads through their owning current authorities. Candidate-local dependencies must still come from the same producer and preview as Retain; otherwise rerun the child.
Finish all fallible read-map and staged-revision merges before mutating carried publication. A caught conflict must leave no commit-capable output behind.
Preview and final replacement use distinct runtime-branded staged-publication capabilities. Output handles, copied structural objects, and preview authority are not commit authority.

Use the store's decision preview only for the prior child outputs and positive candidate dependencies whose Retain decisions gate carry. Resolve that bounded closure lazily through the staged-first, prior-fallback projection; never complete or preflight the whole candidate at each child. Final omission still means withdrawal, and final commit revalidates ordinary reads, currentness, references, envelopes, and producers.

Targeted preview must preserve manifest lineage and callback ordering: validate the exact lifetime of every touched prior entry, snapshot decision descriptors, and seal staged records before slot comparators observe them.

Run domain read rebasers under carry quiescence: they may inspect the supplied preview context but may not read, publish, enter children, commit, or abort through the owning run. Decline carry when another child already staged a prior output.
Finish every external validator and currentness callback before the callback-free descriptor and structural-closure recheck. No callback may run after dependency closure is certified.

Keep structural-reference closure exact and distinct from value consumption. Structural target presence and slot compatibility govern link carry; target value changes activate a consumer only when that consumer also registered an exact or candidate semantic read.
When structural closure changes, a slot comparator may return RefreshWitness to install the fresh detail and fresh closure together; comparator Retain is escalated to Replace.
Resource definition comparison classifies semantic and witness reference subsets inside resources/product-details.ts. Do not duplicate that split in compiler-world, scheduler, or API code.
Until reads declare semantic-versus-witness sensitivity, RefreshWitness activates every reader conservatively. Only Retain may cut propagation in the first queue.

anchors.summary: Exact prior-child carry, read rebase, decision preview, and transactional preflight.
Runtime-branded targeted retention-preview authority, distinct from final replacement authority.
Store-owned rich-detail comparison and changed-closure guard.
Resource semantic-versus-witness comparison authority.
Kernel carry, comparison, structural closure, and atomic replacement doctrine.

records.summary: Each exact project-input read carries its own pull-validated, push-observed, or immutable-snapshot currentness authority.
records.rationale: Exact project-input reads remain the semantic dependency closure, but replaying every filesystem read on each editor request made warm diagnostics and cursor queries perform tens of thousands of host operations. Currentness evidence is heterogeneous inside one generation: an IDE can prove its synchronized open-document values from events while imported dependencies, directory membership, package manifests, and other unproved host inputs still require exact pull validation. Immutable consumer snapshots form a third authority only when their identity names stable input output. Across every revocation or policy transition, evaluator and checker consumers still re-capture exact values before carrying semantic work.
guidance: Keep PullValidated as the default for every mutable host read whose owner cannot prove complete notification for that exact descriptor.

Classify a descriptor as PushObserved only when every mutation affecting it calls advance(); the LSP policy currently applies that proof only to open-document content and existence, not to the surrounding filesystem.
Use SessionSnapshot only when snapshotIdentity names immutable input output, not merely a mutable host session.
Do not replace exact project-input values with event or snapshot identities. Those witnesses avoid redundant validation; exact values still decide semantic carry when a generation is recaptured.
Synchronize policy-mode and snapshot-identity transitions with advance() so a generation cannot observe changed authority before revocation.

anchors.summary: Per-read currentness policy and exact-read validation boundary.
Push-observed authority for synchronized open-document content and existence only.
Workspace watcher ownership for closed admitted source changes.
Project-input generation, exact-read, and change-detection doctrine.
